Eschatology (from Ancient Greek (skhatos) 'last' and -logy) concerns expectations of the end of present age, human history, or the world itself.
Born in Brilon and once a judge and corporate lawyer, this German politician led the CDU as Leader of the Opposition before becoming his country's Chancellor in May 2025 — who is he?
Friedrich Merz (born 11 November 1955) is a German politician who has served as Chancellor of Germany since 6 May 2025.

A wartime RAAF air navigator turned barrister, this Australian Labor leader ran a reformist government that ended with an unprecedented dismissal by the governor-general in 1975 — the only PM ever sacked that way. Who was he?
Gough Whitlam (11 July 1916 - 21 October 2014) was the 21st prime minister of Australia, serving from December 1972 to November 1975.

A veteran of the 1991 Madrid Conference's Palestinian delegation, he went on to serve as Prime Minister of Palestine from 2019 until his 2024 resignation — who is he?
Mohammad Shtayyeh (born 17 January 1958) is a Palestinian politician, academic, and economist who served as the Prime Minister of Palestine from 2019 to 2024.

Philanthropy is a form of altruism that consists of "private initiatives for the public good, focusing on quality of life".

This Indian politician became his country's first-ever president, serving two terms from 1950 to 1962, after being imprisoned by British authorities during both the Salt Satyagraha and the Quit India movement — who is he?

Williamina Fleming is an astronomer. Williamina Paton Stevens Fleming (15 May 1857 – 21 May 1911) was a Scottish astronomer.

Eugene Wigner is a mathematician. Wigner and Hermann Weyl were responsible for introducing group theory into physics, particularly the theory of symmetry in physics.
What is the atomic number of Hassium?
Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
What is the atomic number of Krypton?
Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.
In what year did Werner Heisenberg die?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Ceres discovered?
Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Azithromycin: Pfizer. It is administered by mouth, into a vein, or as topical treatment for the eye.
In which country is Royal Society?
Royal Society: United Kingdom. Founded on 28 November 1660, it was granted a royal charter by King Charles II and is the oldest continuously existing scientific academy in the world.
Who is credited with discovering Caelum?
Caelum: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Caelum SEE-ləm is a faint constellation in the southern sky, introduced in the 1750s by Nicolas Louis de Lacaille and counted among the 88 modern constellations.
Who is credited with discovering 243 Ida?
243 Ida: Johann Palisa. 243 Ida is an asteroid in the Koronis family of the asteroid belt.
Who is credited with discovering Gliese 581d?
Gliese 581d: Stéphane Udry. It was the third planet claimed in the system and the fourth (in a 4-planet model) or fifth (in a disproven 5- or 6-planet model) in order from the star.
Who is credited with discovering Chlorofluorocarbon?
Chlorofluorocarbon: Frédéric Swarts. The most common example of a CFC is dichlorodifluoromethane (R-12).
Sometimes called emotional blindness, this neuropsychological condition involves trouble identifying or describing one's own feelings, and appears in about half of autistic people. What is it?
Alexithymia (-), also called emotional blindness, is a neuropsychological phenomenon characterized by difficulties processing or describing one's emotions.
This type of long-term arthritis causes inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis, with lower back pain as its hallmark symptom. What condition is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.
This medical condition, most often caused in the developed world by liver cirrhosis, is the abnormal buildup of fluid within the abdominal cavity — what is it called?
Ascites is the abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.
Their foliage is almost indistinguishable from a cycad's, but flower-like reproductive organs — some likely insect-pollinated — set these common Mesozoic seed plants apart. Which extinct order?
Bennettitales (also known as cycadeoids) is an extinct order of seed plants that first appeared in the Permian period and became extinct in most areas toward the end of the Cretaceous.
This Russian mathematician-turned-oligarch was worth an estimated $3 billion in 1997 after privatizing state assets like Channel One — yet died impoverished and depressed in 2013. Who was he?
Boris Berezovsky (businessman) (23 January 1946 - 23 March 2013), also known as Platon Elenin, was a Russian business oligarch, government official, engineer and mathematician.
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is commonly spread on roads for de-icing and dust control, and its hygroscopic nature lets it pull moisture straight from the air — what compound is it?
Calcium chloride is an inorganic compound, a salt with the chemical formula CaCl2.
Retired from Istanbul Technical University, this geologist holds foreign membership in both the US and Russian National Academies of Sciences. Who is he?
Celâl Şengör (born 24 March 1955) is a Turkish geologist.
This common name covers many species of bivalve mollusc that use a powerful foot to burrow into sand or mud, with two equal shells joined by adductor muscles — what creature is it?
Clam is a common name for several species of bivalve mollusc. In culinary usage, clams are commonly eaten marine bivalves, as in clam digging and the resulting soup, clam chowder.
This fungal plant disease disfigures maize with galls, yet in Mexican cuisine the infected kernels are prized as huitlacoche, a filling for quesadillas and soups — which disease?
Corn smut is a plant disease caused by the pathogenic fungus Mycosarcoma maydis, synonym Ustilago maydis.
In psychiatry, this is a fixed belief that persists even in the face of clear and obvious evidence to the contrary, distinguishing it from a merely mistaken or strongly held idea — what is it called?
Delusion is a fixed belief that is not amenable to change in light of conflicting evidence.
This unexplained skin condition produces itchy, fluid-filled blisters just millimeters wide on the palms, fingers, or soles, often clearing within a month only to recur — what is it?
Dyshidrosis is a type of dermatitis, characterized by itchy vesicles of 1-2 mm in size, on the palms of the hands, sides of fingers, or bottoms of the feet.
This thin, protective tissue type lines the outer surfaces of organs and the inner surfaces of blood vessels; the skin's outermost layer is a familiar example. What is it?
Epithelium is a thin, continuous, protective layer of cells with little extracellular matrix.
This intracellular protein buffers the body against both iron deficiency and iron overload, and small amounts leak into the blood where doctors measure it as a diagnostic marker — what protein is it?
Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
With about 37 species ranging from central Canada down to Costa Rica, this slender, keeled-scaled reptile typically sports longitudinal stripes in blue, yellow, or red — which reptile is it?
Garter snake is the common name for small to medium-sized snakes belonging to the genus Thamnophis in the family Colubridae.

This Russian mathematician resigned his research post in 2005 and later declared he'd quit the field entirely, disillusioned by its ethical standards, and now lives in seclusion in Saint Petersburg — who is he?
Grigori Perelman (born 13 June 1966) is a Russian mathematician and geometer who is known for his contributions to the fields of geometric analysis, Riemannian geometry, and geometric topology.
With a soft, uncalcified abdomen left dangerously exposed, this crustacean borrows empty snail shells to survive — over 800 species haul their homes around with them. What are they?
Hermit crab are anomuran decapod crustaceans of the superfamily Paguroidea that have adapted to occupy empty scavenged gastropod shells to protect their fragile abdomens.
Triggered by causes like vomiting, diarrhea, or the diuretic furosemide, this condition denotes a blood potassium level under 3.5 mmol/L — what is it?
Hypokalemia is a low level of potassium (K+) in the blood serum.
Native to Africa and Eurasia, which group of opportunistic canid predators includes the black-backed, side-striped, and golden species?
Jackal are canids native to Africa and Eurasia.
This occupation and set of methods involves producing and distributing reports on events and people that make up the 'news of the day,' with a commitment to accuracy — what is it?
Journalism is the production and distribution of reports on events, facts, ideas, and people that constitute the "news of the day" and inform society with a commitment to accuracy and verification.
Shaped by constitutions and produced through statutes, regulations or judicial precedent, this body of enforced rules governs behavior and shapes politics and society — what is it?
Law is a set of rules that are created and enforced by governmental or societal institutions to regulate behavior, with its precise definition a matter of longstanding debate.

Built by an American defense contractor with partners including Northrop Grumman and BAE Systems, this single-engine, single-seat stealth fighter comes in conventional, short-takeoff, and carrier-launched variants — name the aircraft?
Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
An economist by training, he became the only Sikh to lead India and the first prime minister since Nehru to be re-appointed after a full five-year term — who is he?
Manmohan Singh (26 September 1932 - 26 December 2024) was an Indian economist, bureaucrat, academician and statesman who served as the prime minister of India from 2004 to 2014.
Sold dissolved in solution or shipped anhydrous in pressurized railcars, this simplest primary amine reeks like rotten fish — what compound is it?
Methylamine is an organic compound with a formula of CH5N or CH3NH2.
This Bangladeshi economist pioneered microcredit and founded Grameen Bank, work that earned him the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize before he later led an interim government — who is he?
Muhammad Yunus (born 28 June 1940) is a Bangladeshi economist and statesman.
Born in the Austro-Hungarian Empire and emigrating to the US in 1884, he's known for pioneering the AC electricity system. Who?
Nikola Tesla (10 July 1856 - 7 January 1943) was a Serbian-American engineer, futurist, and inventor.
Also covering the modification of facial growth known as dentofacial orthopedics, this branch of dentistry corrects mal-positioned teeth and bite patterns. What field is it?

Orthodontics (also referred to as orthodontia) is a dentistry specialty that addresses the diagnosis, prevention, management, and correction of mal-positioned teeth and jaws, as well as misaligned bite patterns.
This species of hickory tree, native to the Mississippi River region of the southern US and northern Mexico, is the official state nut of five states and the state tree of Texas. What nut is this?
Pecan (pih-KAN,; Carya illinoinensis) is a species of hickory native to the Southern United States and northern Mexico in the region of the Mississippi River.
These drifting, self-feeding members of the plankton community photosynthesize like land plants, so they crowd the sunlit surface waters of oceans and lakes — what are they?
Phytoplankton are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems.
A staple food across the world, this tuber is actually an underground stem from a plant in the nightshade family, with wild relatives growing from the southern U.S. all the way to Chile. What is it?
Potato is a starchy tuberous vegetable native to the Americas that is consumed as a staple food in many parts of the world.
Named partly for the Aztec feathered serpent god and partly for the designer of a tailless aircraft, this genus of giant pterosaur soared over Late Cretaceous North America — what is it?
Quetzalcoatlus is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in North America.
One of the U.S. Air Force's three strategic bombers, this supersonic swing-wing aircraft hauls a 75,000-pound payload and answers to the affectionate name 'Bone' — what is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer is a supersonic variable-sweep wing, heavy bomber used by the United States Air Force.

Sitting near the center of the Milky Way between Libra and Sagittarius, this zodiac constellation's recognition predates Greek civilization, and it was among the 48 catalogued by Ptolemy in the second century — what's the constellation?
Scorpius is a zodiac constellation located in the Southern celestial hemisphere, where it sits near the center of the Milky Way, between Libra to the west and Sagittarius to the east.
Marked by reduced muscle activity yet busy, active brain patterns, this state alternates between REM and non-REM cycles — what is it?
Sleep is a state of reduced mental and physical activity in which consciousness is altered and certain sensory activity is inhibited.
An English dyer and astronomer, this man's 1729 experiments were the first to systematically show that electricity could travel through metals and appear on the surface of insulators — who was he?
Stephen Gray (scientist) (December 1666 - February 1736) was an English dyer and astronomer who was the first to systematically experiment with electrical conduction.
Modern practitioners prioritize common ancestry as they sort living things into ranked taxa, from domain and kingdom all the way down to species — which biological discipline does this?

Taxonomy (biology) (from Ancient Greek (taxis) 'arrangement' and - (-nomia) 'method') is the scientific study of naming, defining (circumscribing) and classifying groups of biological organisms based on shared characteristics.
A staple of Mexican cuisine grown as an annual despite being naturally perennial, this small green-purple fruit is best known for flavoring salsa verde — what is it?
Tomatillo (Physalis philadelphica and Physalis ixocarpa), also known as the Mexican husk tomato, is a plant of the nightshade family bearing small, spherical, and green or green-purple fruit.
This medical condition involves involuntary muscle spasms that interfere with vaginal intercourse or other penetration, often causing pain from the first attempt — what is it?
Vaginismus is a condition in which involuntary muscle spasm interferes with vaginal intercourse or other penetration of the vagina.

This genus of four woody, twining vine species in the legume family is native across East Asia and parts of North America, and became a popular ornamental after being introduced to Europe — what genus is it?
Wisteria is a genus of flowering plants in the legume family, Fabaceae (Leguminosae).
Also known as wattles, this genus of over 1,000 shrub and tree species is now largely reserved for Australian natives — which genus?
Acacia: Genus of plants. Acacia, commonly known as wattles or acacias, is a genus of about 1,084 species of shrubs and trees in the subfamily Mimosoideae of the pea family Fabaceae.
Developed alongside a twinjet sibling by the same European planemaker, this quadjet wide-body airliner entered service in 1993 with launch customers Lufthansa and Air France — which aircraft is it?
Airbus A340: Four-engined twin-aisle airliner family.
Refined from bauxite and nicknamed alumina, this compound shows up in nature as the mineral corundum — the very stuff of rubies and sapphires. What is it?
Aluminium oxide: Chemical compound. Aluminium oxide (or aluminium(III) oxide) is a chemical compound of aluminium and oxygen with the chemical formula Al2O3.
Named for a 19th-century Swedish physicist and symbolized by a letter of the Swedish alphabet, which unit of length equals one ten-billionth of a metre, handy for measuring atoms and bond lengths?
Angstrom: Unit of length. The unit is named after the Swedish physicist Anders Jonas Ångström (1814–1874).
Its name comes from Greek roots meaning 'chief' and 'creator,' and historians often identify whole vanished civilizations by what survives of this visual art. What is it?
Architecture: Art and technique of designing buildings.
A cousin of the tomato and potato, this European nightshade is so toxic — via atropine and scopolamine — that even handling it can harm you; its other common name is "belladonna." What's the plant?
Atropa bella-donna: Deadly nightshade, a flowering plant.
Belonging to genus Fagus, this deciduous tree yields timber used for furniture, flooring, and plywood, and its wood also makes excellent firewood. What is this tree?
Beech: Genus of trees in the family Fagaceae.
Predicted by Einstein's general relativity, this astronomical body is so compact that not even light can escape past its event horizon. What is it?
Black hole: Compact astronomical body. A black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.

This rare and potentially fatal illness comes from a toxin better known by its cosmetic nickname; it starts with blurry vision and slurred speech but usually spares both fever and consciousness — what is it?
First proposed after the 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese, this psychological theory says people are less likely to help a victim when others are present — what's it called?
Bystander effect: Social psychological theory. Recent research has focused on "real world" events captured on security cameras, and the coherency and robustness of the effect has come under question.
These biomolecules often follow the tidy empirical formula (CH2O)n, and as polysaccharides like starch, glycogen, and cellulose they store energy and build structure — what family are they?
Carbohydrate: Organic compound that consists only of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.
Consisting mainly of the brain and spinal cord — and, surprisingly, the retina too — this part of the body integrates information to coordinate an animal's activity — what is it?
Central nervous system: Brain and spinal cord. The rest of this article exclusively discusses the vertebrate central nervous system, which is radically distinct from all other animals.
Patented in 1948, this first-generation antihistamine blocks the H1 receptor to relieve allergy symptoms like hay fever within about two hours — what is it?
Chlorphenamine: Antihistamine used to treat allergies.
First described by Linnaeus in 1758 and introduced to North America to control aphids, this red beetle with seven black spots gets its genus name from the Latin word for 'scarlet' — which species?
Coccinella septempunctata: Species of beetle. It inhabits many regions with a temperate climate.
The first bomber capable of Mach 2 flight, this 1950s delta-winged bomber carried its nuclear payload in a combination bomb-and-fuel pod slung beneath the fuselage — which bomber?
Convair B-58 Hustler: Cold War-era American supersonic bomber.
Caused by prolonged exposure to excess cortisol, this condition produces abdominal weight gain with thin limbs, a rounded red face, and reddish stretch marks — which condition is it?
Cushing's syndrome: Symptoms from excessive exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol.

Known mainly through DNA evidence rather than plentiful fossils, this extinct archaic human group ranged across Asia until about 32,000 years ago, and DNA analysis confirmed the Harbin skull belonged to it — what group is it?
Denisovan: Archaic human species from Asia.
Synthesized from L-DOPA in the brain and kidneys, this catecholamine acts as a neurotransmitter and drives a major brain pathway tied to reward and motivation — what is it?
Dopamine: Organic chemical that functions both as a hormone and a neurotransmitter.
This group of 13 genetic connective tissue disorders causes loose joints and stretchy, velvety skin, with a classification last updated in 2017 — what condition is it?
Ehlers–Danlos syndrome: Group of genetic connective tissues disorders. The existing classification was last updated in 2017, when a number of rarer forms of EDS were added.
Despite never earning a university degree, this German-American psychoanalyst taught at Harvard, Berkeley, and Yale, and coined the term 'identity crisis' — who is he?
Erik Erikson: American psychoanalyst and essayist (1902–1994)

With a red face, a black-and-white head, and a bold yellow wing bar, this small finch native to the Palearctic often appears in Italian Renaissance paintings of the Madonna and Child. What bird is it?
European goldfinch: Species of bird. It has been introduced to other areas, including Australia, New Zealand, Uruguay and the United States.
Also called slapped cheek syndrome, this common childhood illness is caused by parvovirus B19, discovered in 1975 — what condition is it?
Fifth disease: Red rash due to infection with parvovirus B19.
This British-American theoretical physicist lent his name to a hypothetical genetically engineered 'tree' and a transform used in additive number theory — who was he?
Freeman Dyson: British theoretical physicist and mathematician (1923–2020)

Arriving late to a lecture, this mathematician copied down two famous unsolved problems in statistics, mistook them for homework — and solved them; he's better known for inventing the simplex algorithm for linear programming. Who was he?
Known online by the alias 'anakata,' this Swedish computer specialist co-founded a notorious BitTorrent site and later helped WikiLeaks with its 2010 release of a leaked military video — who is he?
Gottfrid Svartholm: Swedish computer specialist. Parts of an interview with Svartholm commenting on the May 2006 police raid of The Pirate Bay are featured in Good Copy Bad Copy and Steal This Film.

Derived independently in the 1830s by two European researchers and later given theoretical backing by George Stokes, this law describes the pressure drop of laminar flow through a drinking straw or a hypodermic needle — what's it called?
Hagen–Poiseuille equation: Law describing the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid.
Nicknamed for its shaggy white spines that dangle over a centimeter long, this edible mushroom is commonly called lion's mane and is used in traditional Chinese medicine — which fungus?
Hericium erinaceus: Edible mushroom. Hericium erinaceus, commonly known as lion's mane, yamabushitake, bearded tooth fungus, or bearded hedgehog, is a species of tooth fungus.
This climbing, hemp-family plant's female cone-shaped flowers are used to flavor and preserve beer — what's the scientific name for hops?
Humulus lupulus: Species of flowering plant.
Formed by the merger of two hip flexor muscles that join at the femur's lesser trochanter, this is the body's strongest flexor of the hip — what is it called?
Iliopsoas: Joined psoas and iliacus muscles of the hip and thigh.
Nicknamed 'Dr. Death,' this pathologist assisted at least 130 patients in dying and was convicted of murder after broadcasting one such case on television — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian: American pathologist and euthanasia activist (1928–2011)
This physician ran the Battle Creek Sanitarium — part spa, part hospital, part luxury hotel — where he treated the rich and poor alike and devised numerous nut and vegetable products — who is it?
Also called Bushman's tea, the leaves of this East African shrub are chewed as a recreational stimulant, most popular among Somalis and Yemenis — what is it?
Closely related to earthworms but equipped with a sucker at each end, these segmented worms are mostly freshwater dwellers, and the medicinal species famously feeds on blood — what are they?
Leech: Parasitic or predatory annelid worms.
A Chinese computer engineer turned science-fiction author, he won the Hugo Award for The Three-Body Problem and the Locus Award for its sequel, Death's End. Who is he?
Liu Cixin: Chinese science fiction writer (born 1963)
First synthesized in 1912 by a Merck chemist, this stimulant known on the street as ecstasy or molly became linked to raves and electronic dance music in the 1980s — which drug?
MDMA: Psychoactive drug, often called ecstasy.
Whether a milk board's 'Got Milk?' campaign or a city pitching itself as a tourist destination, this discipline boils down to acquiring, satisfying, and retaining customers — what is it?
Marketing: Study and process of exploring, creating, and delivering value to customers.
Long before chemists called it 3,4,5-trimethoxyphenethylamine, this psychedelic was drawn from peyote and San Pedro cacti for spiritual ceremonies — which naturally occurring compound is it?
Mescaline: Naturally occurring psychedelic compound. The practice of ingesting mescaline-containing cacti extracts dates back over 6,000 years.
Produced by mammary glands and rich in calcium, protein and lactose, this liquid is often prized for its antibody-packed early form, colostrum — what is it?
Milk: Nutrient-rich liquid produced by mammals.
Its wings make an odd whistling sound on take-off, and one pair may raise up to six broods a year — which abundant North American gamebird?
Mourning dove: North American bird in the family Columbidae.
First identified from an 1856 fossil in a German valley, this group of archaic humans roamed Europe and Asia until vanishing around 40,000 years ago as modern humans arrived — who were they?

As the United States' first swept-wing fighter jet, this Korean War-era aircraft dueled Soviet MiG-15s in some of history's earliest jet-to-jet battles — which plane, produced in more than 7,800 units?
North American F-86 Sabre: Family of US fighter aircraft.
The most arboreal of the great apes, with long arms, short legs and reddish-brown hair, this genus Pongo primate survives today only in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra — what is it?
Orangutan: Genus of Asian apes. The most arboreal of the great apes, orangutans spend most of their time in trees.

Named for its resemblance to a related crested dinosaur, this duck-billed herbivore could grow over 9 meters long, moved on two or four legs, and was first described in 1922 by William Parks — which dinosaur genus?
Parasaurolophus: Hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur genus from Late Cretaceous Period.
Often triggered by a ruptured appendix or a perforated gallbladder, this inflammation of the abdominal lining causes severe pain and swelling — what is it?

Peritonitis: Inflammation of abdominal organ lining. Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.

A counting argument in mathematics: if you have more items than containers, at least one container must hold more than one item. Famous example: three gloves, but only two hand categories — what's this principle?
Pigeonhole principle: If there are more items than boxes holding them, one box must contain at least two items.
Looking like a jellyfish but actually a floating colony of cooperating zooids, this venomous siphonophore is also nicknamed the bluebottle — what is it?
Portuguese man o' war: Species of marine cnidarian.
This holotropical bird family comprises a dozen Afrotropical species and some 167 Neotropical species, including the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which family is this?
Psittacidae: Family of birds. The family Psittacidae or holotropical parrots is one of three families of true parrots.
After his Jewish family fled Germany, this engineer at Sanders Associates dreamed up playing games on a TV screen and built a 'Brown Box' that became the first home video game console — who is he?
Ralph H. Baer: American inventor and engineer (1922–2014)
This English anatomist coined the word 'Dinosauria' — 'terrible reptile' — yet remained an outspoken critic of Darwin's theory of natural selection — who is it?
Richard Owen: English biologist and palaeontologist (1804–1892)
Also known as brewer's or baker's yeast, this single-celled fungus believed to have originated on grape skins is one of biology's most-studied model organisms — which species?
Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Species of yeast. The species has been instrumental in winemaking, baking, and brewing since ancient times.
Comprising seven species from the flatback to the leatherback, five of these ocean-dwelling reptiles are threatened with extinction — what are they?
Sea turtle: Reptiles of the superfamily Chelonioidea.
This small, wingless, primitive insect gets its common name from its grey sheen and darting, fish-like movements — and its scientific name hints at a diet of sugars and starches. What is it?
Silverfish: Small land insect in the order Zygentoma.
This healthcare discipline treats disorders of voice, fluency, and swallowing, practiced by clinicians licensed under boards overseen by groups like ASHA — which field of study?

Named after a Scottish village where it was discovered in 1790, this alkaline earth metal was first isolated in 1808 by Humphry Davy using electrolysis, and identified a year after its discovery by its crimson-red flame test. What element is it?
Strontium: Chemical element with atomic number 38 (Sr)
Turkey's only female prime minister to date, this economist-turned-politician led the country from 1993 to 1996 as head of the True Path Party — who is she?
Tansu Çiller: Prime Minister of Turkey from 1993 to 1996. As a professor of economics, Çiller was appointed Minister of State for the economy by Prime Minister Süleyman Demirel in 1991.

Grain processing strips so much of this micronutrient that many countries enrich their flours to replace it; a deficiency leads to beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy. Also known as vitamin B1, which essential nutrient is it?
Thiamine: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.
This parasite can only complete its sexual reproduction cycle inside cats, and famously manipulates infected rodents into losing their fear of feline scent — what is it?
Toxoplasma gondii: Species of protozoan parasite.
This Timurid sultan who ruled Samarkand spoke five languages and built a great 15th-century observatory there between 1424 and 1429 — who is he?
Ulugh Beg: Timurid sultan, astronomer and mathematician (1394–1449)
This ability to detect light and turn it into an image of one's surroundings can occur via daytime or night vision — what is it called?
Visual perception: Ability to interpret the surrounding environment using light in the visible spectrum.

Caused by the deletion of about 27 genes on chromosome 7, this genetic disorder is known for an unusually outgoing, empathetic personality alongside visual-spatial learning challenges — which condition?
Williams syndrome: Genetic disorder. Williams syndrome (WS), also Williams–Beuren syndrome (WBS), is a genetic disorder that affects many parts of the body.
Fluorine is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for fluorine is F. Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.
What is the chemical symbol for cerium?
The symbol for cerium is Ce. Cerium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ce and atomic number 58, and is a soft, ductile, and silvery-white metal that tarnishes when exposed to air.
